## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shuō wúgòuchēng jīng shū* (T1782) is [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) Kuījī's (632–682 CE) six-fascicle commentary on [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) Xuánzàng's translation of the *Vimalakīrti* ([KR6i0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0077) = T476). Unlike the Tiantai (Zhīyǐ, Zhànrán) and Sānlùn (Jízàng) commentaries which take Kumārajīva's [KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076) as base, Kuījī's commentary uses Xuánzàng's literal Yogācāra-friendly translation. The Taishō header cross-references No. 476.

**Abstract**

Kuījī (632–682 CE) was Xuánzàng's principal Chinese disciple and the systematic founder of the Cí'ēn 慈恩 school of Chinese Yogācāra. After Xuánzàng's death in 664 CE, Kuījī took over the Dàcí'ēn sì 大慈恩寺 translation institute and produced commentaries on the major Yogācāra texts (the *Chéngyùshí lùn* 成唯識論 [T1830, T1831], the *Yùqié shīdì lùn* 瑜伽師地論 [T1829], and many sūtras translated by Xuánzàng).

The *Shuō wúgòuchēng jīng shū* is the principal Yogācāra commentary on the *Vimalakīrti*. Kuījī systematically reads the *Vimalakīrti*'s discourse on non-duality through the *vijñaptimātra* (consciousness-only) framework, showing how the bodhisattva's teaching of emptiness can be reconciled with the *trisvabhāva* (three-natures) doctrine. The result is a Yogācāra hermeneutic that became authoritative in the Cí'ēn school.

The commentary's working dates fall within Kuījī's mature productivity (ca. 660–682 CE). It complements [太賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E8%B3%A2) Tàixián's Korean Yogācāra commentaries on the Yakuṣī cycle ([KR6i0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0053)) — together these texts constitute the consolidated Tang Yogācāra commentarial corpus on the major Mahāyāna sūtras.
